discovery: Theoretical prediction and experimental discovery of topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect
subfield: Condensed matter physics - topological quantum matter
motivation: Kane and Mele showed in 2005 that spin-orbit coupling can produce a new electronic phase, the quantum spin Hall insulator, characterized by a Z2 topological invariant and protected helical edge states, and later generalized this to three-dimensional topological insulators. Molenkamp and co-workers realized this phase in HgTe quantum wells in 2007, observing quantized edge conduction, the first experimental demonstration of a time-reversal-invariant topological insulator. This landmark combination of theory and materials-based experiment opened an entire field: 3D topological insulators, the quantum anomalous Hall effect in magnetic topological heterostructures, Weyl semimetals and topological superconductivity. The concept of symmetry-protected topological band structure now permeates condensed matter physics and has changed how we classify matter, with dissipationless edge channels offering routes to low-energy electronics and topological quantum computation.
